doc.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

title: Rock and roll as an outgrowth of the blues
summary: Brief discussion of 12-bar blues in pop and the blues origins in the Mississippi Delta.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Right. One more question about the early time. I’m wondering, as you learned these songs to play in an R & B band etcetera, was there a moment where you realized oh, this is another 12-bar blues?
Well a lot of the pop music is 12-bar blues, especially at the beginning of what they call rock & roll.

And it goes on today. I think rock & roll was an outgrowth of blues music. And I think blues music probably originated in the Delta in Mississippi. But as things progressed, as the music went to Detroit and went to Memphis, they started changing the rhythms, you know the rock & roll rhythms somehow came into the picture.
